doc.title: Jerry Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe and Christian Goodwillie, via Zoom, June 30, 2021

chapter: Teenage obsession and the record store
title: The teenage bedroom fortress and being the music kid
summary: Gordon describes his obsession at 13: tape recorder, record player and shortwave in his bedroom, and how peers saw him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: You said you were “obsessed.” I mean I read this in an earlier interview. What do you mean by obsessed at that time? How did it manifest itself?

Well currently I’m on the radio on WPRB. Now I do two hours of a show called “Serenade to a Cuckoo” that is 100 percent jazz. But then I do a third hour. And the third hour is a different show. It’s called “Jerry’s Room.” Okay? And in “Jerry’s Room” we play everything but jazz. Okay? And it returns me to my teenage bedroom hiding from my parents, hiding from teachers, hiding from authority, and having all my different electronic equipment going at the same time: my Wollensak tape recorder, my Zenith 200 pound portable record player, my AM/FM shortwave. And this was my young teenage
fortress and where the focus was entirely avoiding homework and listening to music. So the obsession absolutely started when I was 13.
Were you known in junior high and high school as sort of a music nerd? Maybe we didn’t have the word “nerd” at the time, but was that sort of your persona?

No. I wouldn’t say that was my persona but there were those who laughed at the mention of Moby Grape or Vanilla Fudge. There were those who thought like this kid’s out of it. But not a nerd. Maybe crazy. But of course, you know, that was what was happening at the time. It wasn’t for everybody but yes, I followed all the trends and I listened to music closely. Loved it.
